experimentName: What people learn from punishment: A cognitive model (Exp 1)
paper-title: What people learn from punishment: A cognitive model
citation: Radkani, S., Tenenbaum, J. B., & Saxe, R. (2025). What people learn from punishment: A cognitive model. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 122(32), e2500730122. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2500730122
description: Participants read six short scenarios about an authority figure responding to another person's behavior in an unfamiliar society, one scenario in each of six prior-information conditions, assigned by a six-arm Latin square. In every scenario they first report prior beliefs about the wrongness of the act and the authority's justice motive, bias and selfishness, and then report the same beliefs plus the harshness and consequences of the response after learning that the authority chose each of doing nothing, punishing mildly and punishing harshly, in a random order.
